subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close the open conflicting fork PR and allow a fresh narrow fix, or adopt/repair that branch despite its obsolete handler path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the issue has an open closing-reference PR outside the target repository that is conflicting and targets old code, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainer intent is explicit.

options.title: Close and replace the fork PR
options.body: Close https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1564 as obsolete/conflicting, then allow a fresh narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

options.title: Adopt the fork branch manually
options.body: A maintainer can salvage the contributor work by moving the useful behavior onto the active runtime and adding live Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep waiting on the fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on the open fork PR, accepting that the current conflicting branch is not landing-ready.

recommendation.title: Close and replace the fork PR
recommendation.body: Close https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1564 as obsolete/conflicting, then allow a fresh narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mainly repository queue/cleanup ownership, and steipete is the strongest inspected maintainer-routing candidate from adjacent approval SDK history.
